text:
Private credit advances as policy support widens the runway

Rating: overweight

The quiet session on the wire matters more than its silence suggests. Data prints in line, with cpi_now at 2.9% and policy_rate_now holding at 5.00%, giving markets a stable rate backdrop against which private credit can compound. The one_year_return of +11.0% shows the asset class continuing to reward patient capital, while ytd_return of +1.1% suggests the pace has moderated but not reversed. With drawdown at +0.0%, valuations have not needed to absorb any realized stress this cycle — a sign, in our reading, that underwriting discipline and sponsor support are functioning as designed.

The rival house has argued that fragilities are compounding beneath stable marks, pointing to the reported_vs_public_gap of -0.2% as evidence of hidden deterioration. We read the same gap differently: a modest, contained divergence of this size is consistent with normal marking lags between private and public credit, not with concealment. hy_spread_now_bps at 400bps remains a level compatible with orderly conditions rather than distress — spreads that would typically widen sharply ahead of credit events have not done so, and the newsflow reports no defaults or downgrades to substantiate a fragility thesis. In a structurally constructive environment, growth and policy support tend to resolve stress over time rather than let it compound silently.

Our prior does carry a risk: if the reported_vs_public_gap were to widen materially from -0.2% in coming quarters, that could indicate the rival's concern was directionally correct rather than premature. We watch that gap, along with hy_spread_now_bps, as the key signals that would require us to revisit this stance. For now, prudent positioning favors continued exposure, with vigilance rather than complacency guiding the next update.
